title: Notifications: local, remote, the permission and the delegate

videos.script: A reminder the evening before each session. That is all the planner wants from notifications, and it takes four pieces. {{ask}} First, permission. You get one chance to ask, so you ask when the student turns reminders on, not at launch. {{local}} Then a local notification: content, a trigger, and a request whose identifier is the session's own. {{clock}} The trigger is where time goes wrong. A daily reminder at eight, in Lisbon, across the night the clocks go back. One way keeps eight o'clock. The other arrives at seven, every day, for months. You compute both on your own machine. {{delegate}} Then the two moments the app is asked: a notification while it is open, and a tap. {{remote}} And remote notifications, from a server, through Apple. A token that addresses one app on one phone, {{payload}} and a payload with a limit of four kilobytes, which you measure. The framework itself needs a Mac and a phone, and the lesson says so.
